D20·2kq0 — 2026-10-10
chose: 2.2 tasks as branches: a lanes run cuts a run base branch `sofar/<slug>/<run>` from the checkout's HEAD. Each task works on `sofar/<slug>/<run>-<task>`, cut from the run base, in the lane already holding it or else the next clean lane. On task_done the driver commits whatever the session left uncommitted (`.sofar` excluded) on the task branch, gates in the lane, and fast-forwards the run base by compare-and-swap. A landed branch that gets reopened is reset to the base first. Tasks still run one at a time (2.3 adds concurrency), and a branch that cannot fast-forward stops the run with an error note naming the branch (2.4 adds rebase). The stop line names the base for the operator to merge.
over: Moving the checkout's own branch; leaving leftovers uncommitted; reset-to-base on every launch; launching lanes concurrently in 2.2.
because: The checkout's branch is checked out under the operator's working tree and peers' edits (M5), so moving its ref would desync their index. Committing leftovers before the gate makes the verified tree exactly what lands, and a clean checkout of the base then reproduces its fingerprint for the closing sweep. A reopened task that keeps its own branch continues the earlier session's tree, as serial drive does.
